bench_kat_caveat.status: SOURCE DEFECT IN THE BENCH-BUILD BOOT KAT - NOT A CRYPTO PRIMITIVE FAILURE
bench_kat_caveat.root_cause: The reference-vector arrays in bench_kat_run() carry one extra brace level, e.g. 'static const uint8_t s_benchkat_ascon_key[16] = {{0x00, 0x01, ...}};' (main/task_session.c:2610-2620). For an array of uint8_t this initialises element 0 from an over-braced scalar and discards the remaining elements as excess, so every byte after the first is zero. Reproduced independently with gcc -O2 on a minimal case: the compiler emits 'braces around scalar initializer' + 'excess elements in scalar initializer' warnings and the array evaluates to all zeros. The key, nonce and all three expected-output vectors are corrupted the same way, which is why all three KATs fail simultaneously.
bench_kat_caveat.why_it_is_not_the_primitives: The host suite tests the SAME Ascon expected ciphertext (tests/host/test_ascon.c:139 begins 0x77, 0x63, 0xf8, 0xba, 0x6c, 0xe9, 0x1e, 0xd1) and the same X25519 / Ed25519 vectors, and passes. The device and host therefore use identical vectors and differ only in the initialiser defect, not in codegen or toolchain behaviour.
bench_kat_caveat.impact: Informational only. bench_kat_run() is compile-gated, is documented in-code as 'a log line, never a gate', and gates nothing: no registry value, paper number, or sealed capture depends on its result. The timed BENCHPRIM samples are taken independently and every sample reports err=0.
bench_kat_caveat.reading_rule: Anyone (human or log pipeline) who flags this line must not read it as an Ascon/X25519/EdDSA failure. No entry in this registry is derived from the boot KAT.
bench_kat_caveat.corrective_action: Deliberately NOT applied: fixing the initialisers would change the firmware image and therefore the provenance of the already-sealed bench runs (image e1ca1b5a...). Recorded here as a known limitation of the bench builds.

entries.description: OPEN DEFECT (intermittent): transport_ble BLE context mutex handling can panic the ESP32 and reboot the board during the IDLE-phase entry that immediately precedes the post-derive-sync barrier. The ble_ctx_lock deadlock detector trips when the lock is held by the pair_supp task for >2000 ms, and the following lock timeout leads to a FreeRTOS assertion (xTaskPriorityDisinherit, tasks.c:5156 - disinheriting a mutex not held by the current task). Field symptom: inexplicable ~45 s extra pairing delay followed by success on retry. Observed on the E1-A binary only (1 of 4 captured runs).
entries.value: 1 occurrence in 4 captured runs (E1_A_plain_20261018, canonical Device B = this session's merged-log tag [DEVICE_A], host 14.5 s)

source.status: PARTIALLY ADDRESSED IN TREE (uncommitted, compile-verified; NOT hardware-verified) - 2026-10-19 update. Chain: illegal release removed (FIX-BLE-CTX-LOCK-RELEASE); 26 unguarded call sites hardened (FIX-BLE-LOCK-CALLSITE-HARDENING); >2 s watchdog hold removed (FIX-BLE-ADV-WATCHDOG-LOCK-HOLD); and the lock-held advertising re-arm in the disconnect path (the site independently verified lock-held in .agents/BLE_LOCK_AUDIT_FINDINGS.md 1) now defers via s_adv_restart_pending and drains after unlock through transport_ble_service_pending_adv_restart(). Evidence: sealed E1_A_plain_20261019 rerun (480 s, 160/160 BENCH58 TX) - no panic/abort/assert/watchdog reset; one adv-watchdog W line (advertising down 2473 ms, phase=SIGN_PK_EXCHANGE); the deferral fingerprint had 0 hits (path NOT exercised). Defect remains OPEN pending a hardware run that exercises the path; the remaining start_advertising call sites are not fully audited (.agents/BLE_LOCK_AUDIT_FINDINGS.md 5).

entries.description: Fix for BUG-BLE-CTX-LOCK-PANIC. ble_ctx_lock() returns false when its 2 s take times out, but ble_ctx_unlock() called xSemaphoreGive() unconditionally, so a caller that timed out released a mutex it never held. FreeRTOS then attempted to priority-disinherit a mutex the current task did not own, tripping the assertion at tasks.c:5156 and rebooting the board. ble_ctx_unlock() now releases only when the current task is the recorded owner (s_ble_ctx_lock_owner == xTaskGetCurrentTaskHandle()); a timing-out caller becomes a correct no-op.
entries.value: illegal release path removed by construction; NOT yet built, flashed, or reproduced on hardware

source.status: APPLIED AND COMPILE-VERIFIED ONLY - not flashed and not observed on hardware, and the intermittent race cannot be reproduced on demand. All 26 call sites that ignored the false return are now hardened (see FIX-BLE-LOCK-CALLSITE-HARDENING). The separate >2 s hold that made the timeout reachable is addressed by FIX-BLE-ADV-WATCHDOG-LOCK-HOLD.

entries.description: Hardening of the 26 call sites in transport_ble.c that discarded ble_ctx_lock()'s return value and then used g_ble_ctx as if the lock were held. Previously a caller whose 2 s take timed out proceeded into the critical section with no mutual exclusion - a data-corruption defect independent of the panic, and one that would still exist after the crash fix alone. Each site now uses the guarded pattern already present at transport_ble_connect_to_peer: abort the operation with a warning instead of continuing unlocked. The bail value matches each function's return type.
entries.formula: if (!ble_ctx_lock()) { ESP_LOGW(TAG, "<fn>: ble_ctx_lock timed out - skipping"); return <type-appropriate bail>; }
entries.value: 26 sites hardened; the file then has 30 guarded sites and 0 unguarded sites (26 new + the 4 that already checked the return value)

source.status: compile-verified only: ninja exit=0, transport_ble.c.obj rebuilt and newer than its source, image ceepew.bin 0x1573b0 bytes with 31% of the app partition free, brace balance 0. NOT flashed and NOT run on hardware. Caveat: the two state getters now return a conservative default (0U / PAIRING_PHASE_IDLE) when the lock cannot be taken, which is safe but is not equivalent to a successful read - callers treat an unreadable phase as 'not pairing'.

entries.description: Root cause of the >2 s ble_ctx_lock hold that made BUG-BLE-CTX-LOCK-PANIC reachable, found by locating what the holder task actually does while holding the lock. The task named pair_supp is transport_ble_supervisor_task (xTaskCreate at transport_ble.c:4226). Its tick calls transport_ble_supervisor_tick_adv_watchdog(), which took ble_ctx_lock() and then, while still holding it, called transport_ble_start_advertising(). That function reaches the BLE controller through transport_ble_configure_data_raw_unlocked(): esp_ble_gap_stop_advertising() (components/bt/host/bluedroid/api/esp_gap_ble_api.c:147), esp_ble_gap_config_adv_data_raw() (:618) and esp_ble_gap_config_scan_rsp_data_raw() (:642). CORRECTION (checked against IDF v6.0.3 source, 2026-10-19): an earlier revision of this entry said those calls 'block until the controller acknowledges'. That mechanism description is wrong. They are asynchronous queue posts, not controller-ACK waits: each calls btc_transfer_context() (components/bt/common/btc/core/btc_task.c:372) -> btc_task_post(msg, OSI_THREAD_MAX_TIMEOUT) -> osi_thread_post() (components/bt/common/osi/thread.c:338) -> osi_thead_work_queue_put() (:114), where OSI_THREAD_MAX_TIMEOUT == OSI_SEM_MAX_TIMEOUT == 0xffffffff (components/bt/common/osi/include/osi/semaphore.h:27) selects xQueueSend(wq->queue, item, portMAX_DELAY) at thread.c:122, and thread.h:56 documents that sentinel as 'blocking forever'. The hold is therefore unbounded and gated on BTC work-queue capacity rather than on controller responsiveness - which makes the >2 s hold easier to reach, not harder, and does not change the fix or its location. The watchdog only runs when advertising has been down for >=2 s, i.e. precisely when the controller may be unresponsive, so the hold can exceed the 2 s lock timeout - which is what made enter_phase() time out and report the holder as pair_supp. The watchdog now evaluates its condition and updates its state under the lock, releases the lock, and only then performs the re-arm.
entries.formula: lock -> read state, decide need_rearm, update s_adv_down_since_ms -> unlock -> transport_ble_start_advertising()
entries.value: long hold removed from the supervisor/watchdog path; the blocking radio calls now execute with no lock held

entries.description: One-way radio latency (E5), measured with a microsecond sync pulse on a single jumper wire between GPIO14 of both boards (open-drain, assert-low, falling edge timed). The transmitter asserts the line immediately before esp_now_send; the receiver timestamps the edge against its own esp_timer, so both endpoints of the interval lie on the receiver's clock and no cross-board clock correction is used or needed. This is the headline E5 figure.
entries.formula: edge_to_rxcb = t_rxcb - t_edge  (both timestamps on the receiver's own esp_timer_get_time() epoch)

source.status: single bench run, one board pair, 20 cm, channel 1, hopping off, 115200 baud. Medians and IQRs quoted as robust statistics; the DEVICE_B maximum is a stale-latch artifact (see EXP-E5-STALE-EDGE) and is NOT excluded.

entries.description: Transmitter-side stages preceding the sync pulse (E5). submit->pulse is the interval from the campaign submitting frame n to the pulse being asserted (= the on-device cryptographic and ARQ framing path); pulse->sendcb is from the pulse being asserted to the ESP-NOW send callback firing. Both are same-clock intervals on the transmitting board. Reporting these separately is what makes the crypto cost distinguishable from the radio cost.
entries.formula: submit_to_pulse = t_pulse - t_submit ; pulse_to_sendcb = t_sendcb - t_pulse  (same board clock)

source.status: TX sequence coverage is complete and exact on both boards: seq 0..79, unique=80, gaps=0.

entries.description: Receiver-side processing after the ESP-NOW receive callback (E5): rxcb->accept is the interval from frame delivery to the callback to the frame being accepted into the session layer. Consistent with the independently measured Ed25519 verify plus Ascon decrypt cost.

source.status: DEVICE_B maximum is a stale-latch artifact (265880.270 ms), not excluded; median and IQR are robust to it.

entries.description: Measurement limitation in the E5 report that must be disclosed whenever E5 sequence coverage is cited. The RX-side seq field is read from the first byte of the ARQ-decoded frame at the receive-callback hook, which is an internal header byte, NOT the BENCH58 campaign sequence number. It reports a constant 69 on both boards, so the report's RX sequence-coverage lines (unique=1, gaps=0) are void and are not evidence of duplicate or missing frames.
entries.value: RX seq reported as 69..69, unique=1 on both DEVICE_A and DEVICE_B; TX seq valid at 0..79, unique=80, gaps=0

source.status: Does NOT affect the headline edge->rxcb interval: the accept hook reads the same variable within the same process_rx_frame call, so the pairing is self-consistent.

entries.description: Measurement artifact in E5, reported rather than removed. The sync-line ISR latches an edge; if no receive callback consumes it (for example a frame rejected before the callback), the stale latch is consumed by a much later frame, inflating that record's edge->rxcb interval. Affects 1 of 68 DEVICE_B receive records.
entries.value: DEVICE_B edge->rxcb max = 341336.571 ms and rxcb->accept max = 265880.270 ms, both from the same stale-latch mechanism

entries.description: Authoritative rejection breakdown for the sealed E2b forged-frame run, recorded to stop a working note from being cited as replay evidence. Earlier working notes described E2b as containing '2 replay' rejections among 36. Re-reading the sealed capture shows those two lines are 'ESL transport header/MAC/replay check failed (err=3 len=2)' - a conflated message covering ESL header failure, MAC failure AND the ESL replay sub-check - and it is NOT CEEPEW_ERR_REPLAY. A third line is an ARQ-layer '[ARQ_RX] REPLAY reject', which is Stop-and-Wait duplicate suppression at the link layer and must NOT be counted as a cryptographic replay defence. No err=17 rejection was observed anywhere in E2b.
entries.value: err=5: 34 lines; err=3 (conflated ESL header/MAC/replay check): 2 lines; ARQ-layer replay reject: 1 line; replay-window commit rejection (the message "replay commit rejected"): 0 lines. A bare substring match for '(err=17)' is NOT a valid detector: it matches exactly 1 line, capture_dual.log:2172, which is the ARQ duplicate-sequence path returning the same error value.

source.site: main/task_session.c:2067 (the err=17 release path) versus the ESL stage's conflated err=3 message
source.status: CORRECTION to an unsealed working note only - no registry entry ever asserted E2b replay rejections, and the forged-frame result (EXP-FORGE-REJECT-MODEC, 16/16 per run) is unaffected. Consequence: E2b does NOT provide on-device replay-rejection evidence; that is what E3 exists to produce. Any future analyzer must not match replay injections on err=17 alone or it will report a false 'defence failed' verdict when the ESL layer catches the replay with err=3. Confirming evidence for that warning, verified 2026-10-19: a bare '(err=17)' text match over the sealed E2b log returns exactly one line - capture_dual.log:2172 '[SECURE_CHAT_RX] ARQ decode failed / duplicate sequence (err=17)' - i.e. the link-layer ARQ path, not the replay window. The zero count stated in "value" is therefore a claim about the replay-window commit-rejection message specifically, and must not be paraphrased as 'E2b contains no err=17 lines'.

Pre-registered acceptance checks: (1) DUT frames captured - PASS; (2) literal 0x41 application marker visible on air - FAIL; (3) mode_report verdict recorded - PASS. Per the pre-registered rule, the check-2 failure is an APPARATUS/DESIGN failure of the acceptance test, not a negative result about the Mode-A claim.
entries.value: 2/3. DUT-frame census: A pcap 93 frames = 91 from DUT B + 2 non-DUT; B pcap 94 = 91 from DUT A + 3 non-DUT. Max 0x41 run = 1 byte in every captured frame (both devices). mode_report (both devices): application plaintext is NOT VISIBLE on air in this mode - pooled payload 7953 B (A) / 8083 B (B); entropy 6.7865 / 6.7927 bits/B; printable-ASCII 37.26% / 37.15%; marker hits 0/93 and 0/94. Check 2 is unsatisfiable on the current pipeline: messages are Huffman-compressed unconditionally (main/session_send.c step 1) before FEC, and FEC parity positions are keyed - literal application bytes cannot appear on air.
